api-errors.reason: ApiProblem and ThalovantError's api_problem/api_code/api_detail live in src/errors.rs; api_response_error() in src/control.rs parses every failure body once and fills ApiResponse.problem, leaving the bounded, redacted display line as it was, and ApiProblem's hand-written Debug redacts secret-named keys so {:?} and an unwrap() panic cannot print an echoed password. tests/api_errors.rs serves each shared vector from a loopback HTTP peer, reads it back through ControlPlane::get_hub and records what it produced through tests/common/mod.rs, which is hashed beside it because it controls canonicalisation.

Run against the shared binary vectors and against binary-frames.json, which is hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output rather than frames this SDK built for itself.

connection-admission.reason: wait_for_admission in src/control.rs polls GET /v1/operations/{id} (the OperationResource id, else the id at the end of links.self), every read bounded by the deadline: ready, no operation and 404 are admitted; failed and timed_out are ThalovantError::AdmissionFailed with the operation's error_code and no status; a 401 or 403 is returned as the ApiResponse it is (api_refusal says Auth); any other refusal of the wait is AdmissionFailed with no error_code, keeping status and problem; a 5xx is ridden out; a 429 waits the problem's retry_after_seconds (top level or inside a detail object), else the Retry-After header, else RateLimit-Reset (read from the response by get_with_retry_after, since ApiResponse keeps no headers), or the poll interval when longer, and one asking for longer than is left is AdmissionTimeout at once; the deadline is AdmissionTimeout, whose message ends 'it may still admit it later', for which is_timeout() and is_connection_error() in src/errors.rs are both true. An API out of reach is ApiUnreachable, returned as it is. An absolute links.self on another origin (scheme, host, port with default ports) than the API's is ThalovantError::Api and never fetched. tests/home_link.rs serves each case's exchanges from a loopback HTTP peer with the case's headers, fills {api_host}/{api_port}, points 'unreachable' cases at a closed port, checks every request, requires every exchange to be used, and records through tests/common/mod.rs -- hashed beside it because it controls canonicalisation -- before asserting.

connection-kinds.reason: create_client_identity_of_type sends spec.connection_type and spec.version, deletes a client whose answer does not echo the kind (DELETE with If-Match: the answer's etag) and fails with ThalovantError::UnsupportedConnectionType, as it does for a 422 naming connection_type in its detail or code or in a validation error's loc or msg (under errors, or under detail when that is a list), never in the rest of the body, which echoes the request; get_client and delete_client (etag read first when none is given, one retry on 412, 404 is deleted) live in src/control.rs. Refusals are not retyped: an existing call still returns ThalovantError::ApiResponse, and ThalovantError::api_refusal() in src/errors.rs classifies Auth (401, 423, 403 Insufficient scopes), Plan (402, 403 plan_limit) and AlreadyLinked (409 home_assistant_already_linked, with linked_client_id() read from client_id/existing_client_id/connection_id, top level then nested detail). The runner asserts every refusal it classifies is still ApiResponse. tests/home_link.rs serves each case's exchanges from a loopback HTTP peer, in order, through the real ControlPlane path, checks every request's method, path, body or body subset, If-Match and Authorization, requires every exchange to be used, and records what it produced through tests/common/mod.rs -- hashed beside it because it controls canonicalisation -- before asserting.

Rust unit tests are colocated with their implementation; complete tested modules are recorded as test evidence and exports/delegates as implementation evidence. device-login.reason: begin_device_login (an empty scope list left out), poll_device_login (one POST /v1/auth/device/token, returning the ApiToken or ThalovantError::DeviceLoginPending with the interval -- lengthened by five seconds for good per device code, kept in the control plane's private device_intervals -- DeviceLoginExpired or DeviceLoginDenied, each with the status and boxed problem) and revoke_api_token live in src/control.rs; revoking the token in use treats the API's 401 as revoked and forgets it, revoking again sends nothing until the next sign-in (a private flag every sign-in clears), and every sign-in sets token_id from its own answer; the variants and their status_code/api_problem answers in src/errors.rs. home-link.reason: src/home.rs holds HOME_REQUEST/HOME_RESPONSE, HOME_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, RESPONSE_TYPES and ERROR_CODES (asserted equal to the vector file's lists), HomeRequest, HomeAnswer, home_response, plain_speech (src/rich.rs strip_ssml removes only real tags, comments and processing instructions; decode_references decodes numeric references, the five XML entities and   and nothing else; Unicode White_Space collapses), and answer_home_request/answer_home_request_within: everything within the hub's 10 s counted from the call, the handler on a spawned task given min(timeout, what is left) and answered timeout at the deadline while it is left to finish, the reply given what the handler left, never started after the bound and withdrawn when it passes (None when there was no time). reply_context is in src/events.rs (a destination with no source gives no destination), Client::reply in src/client.rs, replying from Event::context as the hub sent it. src/transport.rs holds close_refuses (1000/1005/1008 during the handshake or within 750 ms after it, a code learnt up to 250 ms late) and the typed handshake verdicts: a message that fails to authenticate and a refusal close are HubRefused, a pin mismatch HubKeyChanged, and a failed KK is followed at once by one XX in the same connect; runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. Rust unit tests are colocated with their implementation; complete tested modules are recorded as test evidence and exports/delegates as implementation evidence. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs.
